chapter.title: COM Objects (Windows)
chapter.para: On Windows, the bridge also reaches COM objects (Excel, Word, the Scripting objects, WMI, any automation server) through IDispatch, late-bound, as ooRexx's own OLEObject and C#'s dynamic reach them, and with the same Rexx syntax as any NetObject. A program written for OLEObject changes little to use the bridge (), and gets .NET in the same program: its collections, its dates, Windows Forms.

section.title: Creating and Using COM Objects
section.para: .net~createObject(progid) creates a COM object (). It is a NetObject whose messages are those of IDispatch: by name, caseless, as a method call or a property read (servers take either); o~Name = v sets a property; o[i] and o[i] = v are the default member; DO OVER enumerates a COM collection. The COM objects that a COM object returns are such objects too. An unknown name is SYNTAX 97.1; any other failure, SYNTAX 98.900 with the COMException.
.net~releaseObject(o) releases the object at once, so that its server (an Excel process) can end now rather than at .NET's next collection.

example.title: A COM object
example.programlisting:
d = .net~createObject("Scripting.Dictionary") d~Add("a", 1); d~Add("b", "two") say d~Count d~Item("b") d~ITEM("b") d~Exists("a") d~Exists("zz") d~Add("z", .net~box("string", "007")); d~Add("n", "007") say d~Item("z") d~Item("n") say d~Keys~items d["b"]
::requires "net.cls"

section.title: Arguments
section.para: A COM method declares VARIANT parameters, which say nothing about the value they want, so the bridge sends what OLEObject sends:

listitem.para: &true; and &false; themselves, and a Boolean (): booleans (VT_BOOL).
A Rexx number: an int if it is whole and fits in 32 bits, else a double. So "007" is 7; .net~box("string", "007") keeps the text.
An Array: a SAFEARRAY of its rank, its items converted the same way (Excel: range~Value = grid, a two-dimensional Array).
An omitted argument, and &nil;: "not given", for the method's optional parameters (fso~OpenTextFile(file, , .true)).
A NetRef: by reference, as an OLEVariant (ADO's conn~Execute(sql, n), then n~value).
.net~named(name, value): a named argument, VBA's name:=value, anywhere among the others: excel~Workbooks~Open(file, .net~named("ReadOnly", .true)). OLEObject has none.

section.para: A result that is VT_NULL or VT_EMPTY is &nil;, as with OLEObject (WMI answers it for properties without a value).

The language of each call. Every call is made in English (US), as VBA makes them, so Excel reads =SUM(...) on any Windows. .net~createObject(progid, "user") makes the calls in the user's language instead, as OLEObject does (a Spanish Windows: =SUMA(...)), and a culture name ("es-ES") in that one; the objects it returns keep that language.
A busy server (Excel with a dialog open) refuses calls for a while: the bridge tries again, waiting longer each time, for up to 10 seconds, as VBA does, before it raises the error.

section.title: Objects That Already Exist
section.para: .net~getObject(moniker) is the object a moniker names, as OLEObject's GetObject and VBA's GetObject(path) give it: a document (opened by its application), or WMI through "winmgmts:". .net~getActiveObject(progid) is the running instance of a class (VBA's GetObject(, "Excel.Application")): an Excel opened by hand; an error if none runs. Office registers itself as running when it is started by hand, not when it is started by automation. Both take the language as createObject does.

example.title: WMI through a moniker
example.programlisting:
wmi = .net~getObject("winmgmts:\\.\root\cimv2") do os over wmi~ExecQuery("select Caption, Version from Win32_OperatingSystem") say os~Caption os~Version end
::requires "net.cls"

section.title: Constants and Type Information
section.para: .net~getConstant(o, name) is a constant of the type library that o comes from, as OLEObject's o~getConstant(name): .net~getConstant(excel, "xlHAlignRight"), caseless, &nil; if there is none; .net~getConstant(o) gives them all, a StringTable. Each library has its own: DAO's dbText comes with a DAO object, not with Access.Application.

.net~getKnownMethods(o) and .net~getKnownEvents(o) give the same stems as OLEObject's getKnownMethods and getKnownEvents, from the object's type information; the first also has !PROGID and !CLSID, OLEObject's progid and clsid. .net~events(o) lists the names of the events.

example.title: Type library constants
example.programlisting:
fso = .net~createObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject") say .net~getConstant(fso, "ForAppending") .net~getConstant(fso, "temporaryfolder") say .net~getConstant(fso, "NoSuchConstant") temp = fso~GetSpecialFolder(.net~getConstant(fso, "TemporaryFolder")) say fso~FolderExists(temp~Path)
::requires "net.cls"

section.title: Events
section.para: A COM object's events are .NET events, with the same syntax: o~Name += h, o~Name -= h, .net~addHandler(o, "Name", h), any object and method, added and removed at any time (OLEObject instead calls methods of the object itself, made "WITHEVENTS"). The method gets the event's parameters; one passed by reference arrives as a Rexx.Net.ComRef, and ref~Value = x gives the event's source a new value when the method returns: Excel's Cancel.

COM delivers the events of another process (Excel) to a Rexx thread while that thread waits in .NET: during a call to the COM object (the events it causes), in .net~nextEvent(seconds), or in .net~eventLoop. Where an OLEObject program waits with call SysSleep 1, wait with .net~nextEvent(1). Every Rexx thread that uses the bridge is a single-threaded apartment (STA), as .NET's user interface threads and PowerShell's are ().

example.title: Excel's events, one of them cancelled
example.programlisting:
excel = .net~createObject("Excel.Application") w = .Watcher~new excel~SheetChange += .net~handler(w, "CHANGED") excel~WorkbookBeforeClose += .net~handler(w, "CLOSING") book = excel~Workbooks~Add book~Worksheets~Item(1)~Range("A1")~Value = 42 -- SheetChange, during the call book~Close(.false) -- refused by CLOSING say excel~Workbooks~Count excel~DisplayAlerts = .false; excel~Quit; .net~releaseObject(excel)
::requires "net.cls" ::class Watcher ::method changed use arg sheet, range say "changed:" range~Address ::method closing use arg book, cancel cancel~Value = .true

section.title: From OLEObject

row.entry: o~method(args), o~property, o~property = v, o[i], DO x OVER o
a string that must stay a string
the user's language for every call
drop o (released at the next collection)

section.para: The project's samples/office has Excel, Word and PowerPoint programs written twice, with OLEObject and through the bridge, events included; samples/oorexx-ole has the OLE samples that come with ooRexx for Windows, through the bridge.
